expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint
expectations.evidence: Diagnosis is correct ('they never recompute the hash from the block's contents... the stored hash field is just copied along with the tampered data'), but the agent dumped a complete multi-milestone implementation instead of coaching the current milestone: wrote a full 3067-char blockchain.py containing Block with calculate_hash, mine()/PoW, genesis, add_block, is_valid and a __main__ demo — a whole build-your-own-blockchain, far beyond the minimal validation fix the user needed.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Concrete command with expected output shown: 'python3 blockchain.py' → 'honest chain valid: True / tampered chain valid: False / re-hashed chain valid: False' ('Wrote blockchain.py and ran it — output confirms the fix').

expectations.text: B3: Explains you must recompute each block's hash and compare to its stored hash, not only compare stored links
expectations.evidence: 'validation must recompute each block's hash from its actual contents (data + prev_hash + timestamp + nonce etc.) and compare to the stored hash field'; 'Nothing in your validator ever asks: "does this hash actually match this block's contents?"'

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: Only shell command run was 'python3 blockchain.py'; single write to project file blockchain.py; no install commands (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install/gem install) and nothing written outside the project dir.
